# Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Proposal for Tamarack Instruments**
Prepared for Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (Sponsor)

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The Client is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff. Revenue was described in discovery as "in the US$200 to 300 million range." That figure comes from the conversation, not from filings. The Client has not completed a prior AI Governance Academy program, so this proposal starts from the position recorded in the discovery call notes of 6 October 2026.

The Client's AI portfolio spans three lifecycle stages:

* A customer service chatbot is deployed on the support portal.
* AI visual inspection is in pilot on the German production line.
* AI sales forecasting is planned for next year.

AI maturity is stated as Piloting. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that no inventory of AI systems exists.

The Client lists three incumbent frameworks:

* An ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS.
* An ISO 9001 quality management system.
* An internal audit function.

The Profile Block does not describe the registers, processes, controls or records held within these. The extent to which existing management system artifacts can be reused for AI governance is therefore Unknown and will be confirmed at intake.

The stated objective is direct: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." ISO/IEC 42001 is a certification target, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed and is rendered Unknown.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory

At Piloting maturity, governance has to keep pace with three use cases at different stages. It also has to keep pace with a production date and a management system standard whose preparation has yet to begin. A one-time assessment would capture the position at a single point in time. A fractional advisor provides continuity as each of these moves.

The engagement is guided by three principles:

* **Slow AI:** governance decisions are taken at a deliberate pace, ahead of deployment rather than after it.
* **Informed Intent:** each use case enters production with a documented understanding of its purpose, risks and controls.
* **Final Liability rests with the Human:** the Client's people own every decision. The advisor informs those decisions but does not make them.

The engagement works from two frameworks:

* The GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for registers, controls and evidence.
* The Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for deliberate use case intake and review.

Executive and board reporting draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. Annual Arc

**Timing inputs flagged for intake**

| Input | Status |
|---|---|
| Engagement start date | Unknown |
| Visual inspection production target | Q2 2027 (stated) |
| ISO/IEC 42001 start date | Unknown, not fixed |
| ISO/IEC 42001 certification audit date | Unknown |
| Applicability and timing of EU AI Act obligations to each use case | Flagged for verification by counsel |

The arc places visual inspection governance in the first half of the engagement and ISO/IEC 42001 readiness in the second. If the start date leaves less than two quarters before production in Q2 2027, Quarters 1 and 2 will be compressed. The Sponsor will then be asked to set priorities.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize**

* Respond to the June 2026 audit finding by establishing an AI system inventory, using the GRC Workbook register structure.
* Define governance roles and decision rights. Role holders are Unknown and will be named by the Client.
* Set a policy baseline.
* Open a Slow AI Kitchen intake for the visual inspection pilot.

**Quarter 2: Deepen**

* Prepare visual inspection for production. This covers risk assessment, human oversight design, data handling review and go-live criteria for the Client to approve.
* Flag the EU AI Act and GDPR questions arising from the use case to counsel for verification.
* Align governance artifacts with the outcome of any works council consultation. The Client stated that the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff. Whether that consultation applies to this deployment, and when, is Unknown and is for the Client and counsel to determine.

**Quarter 3: Assure**

* Begin ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work. This covers a gap assessment, an evidence collection plan and an internal audit approach for the AI management system.
* Confirm at intake how this work relates to the existing ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 systems.
* Apply the constraint that customer data stays in the EU to each in-scope use case.

**Quarter 4: Evolve**

* Run the planned sales forecasting use case through Slow AI Kitchen intake before build.
* Mature registers and evidence toward ISO/IEC 42001 readiness.
* Report to the executive team using AI Governance for Boards.
* Prepare the Month 11 renewal and handover review.

All audit preparation is expressed in readiness terms. No certification or audit outcome is promised.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

The engagement runs on four fixed elements:

* A monthly executive advisory session.
* A monthly working session with the governance team.
* Asynchronous availability for defined question categories.
* A quarterly governance review.

The Profile Block lists these roles of interest:

* General Counsel
* CISO
* Head of Quality
* Head of Data
* German plant manager
* Two internal auditors

Attendance at each session is Unknown and will be set by the Sponsor. Response windows and escalation paths for asynchronous questions will be agreed in the first month.

## 5. Scope

**In scope:**

* Governance evolution
* Implementation guidance
* Audit preparation
* AI strategy
* Executive decision support

**Out of scope:**

* Legal advice
* Certification body functions
* Staff augmentation
* Incident command

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including regulatory interpretation under the EU AI Act and GDPR, route to external counsel.

## 6. Investment

The fee is US$10,000 per month for a twelve-month term, or US$120,000 in total. The term is renewable.

The Client stated a budget approval of up to US$80,000 for this fiscal year. At US$10,000 per month, that covers up to eight months of fees within the current fiscal year. The Client's fiscal year dates are Unknown, as is the engagement start date. How the term falls across fiscal years is therefore flagged for confirmation with the Sponsor before signature.
